summary: Sense 1: revise the gloss
before: ackern, pflügen (mit ʕal), speziell das zweite Ackern nach dem krōwo, dem Aufackern des Brachlandes, mit den Furchen senkrecht zu dem krowo;
after: ackern, pflügen (Zugtier mit ʕal, b-; Acker als direktes Objekt); auch das zweite Ackern nach dem krōwo, dem Aufackern des Brachlandes, mit den Furchen senkrecht zu dem krowo
rationale: 94/74 explicitly has one pass, while 94/111 coordinates dwr with first ploughing krw. The special second operation is not an exclusive lexical requirement. MAC Old lady and a bird/31 adds b- for draught animals; cultivated ground is a direct object in JL and Ritter.

summary: The single-pass statement at 94/74 and first-ploughing coordination at 94/111 show that dwr is broader than the special second orthogonal pass. Preserve the special operation as a use, while clarifying the general gloss.

Cultivated ground is an unmarked object; crops can also be objects in ploughing-in contexts. Draught animals appear with ʕal and b-. These frames distinguish participants without requiring new meanings.

Existing I.2 to farm covers sharecropping, paid farming, and broad cultivation. Payment bḥaq and share bsahmo are ordinary manner/remuneration adjuncts, not fixed idioms. Vineyard objects alone do not force I.2 when the text explicitly says ploughing.

The glossary files occupational daworo/dawore under Part act.; retain that recall convention, while noting that habitual profession predicates may be lexical nouns rather than productive verbal predications.

dworo action nouns occur as purpose, source, activity subject and land-measure complement. These are active Infinitiv contexts; the inherited Detransitive section conflates them with genuine crop-patient Infectum mədwori at 6/52.

No III textual occurrence was supplied, so the existing causative entry remains unchanged. Source mismatches EL 12/Hors 1/12, JL 10.10.1/JL 10.11/1 and PrS page/line versus text/verse numbers are retained for editorial concordance checks.
